sessions.title: Session dashboard redesign
sessions.purpose: Rebuild the home and session views so status is readable at a glance
sessions.sinceLast: Edited 3 files, ran the test suite, now fixing 1 failing test

stream.text: Yesterday · 10:58 PM
The home screen makes no sense. An orbit diagram in the middle, one card far left, one far right. Redesign home and the session view so I can see what every session is doing at a glance.

stream.summary: Mapped the current layout and what each screen needs to answer
stream.text: The user wants scannability over decoration. Every session should answer four things: what it is, what changed, its state, and what to do next. The orbit carries none of that, so it can go. I'll audit the current components before proposing anything.

stream.markdown:
## What's wrong today

I read the five files that drive these two screens. The problems are structural, not cosmetic:

| Area | Problem | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Orbit diagram takes 60% of the screen | Session cards pushed to the far edges |
| Home | Only 2 cards visible, no grouping | Can't tell what needs you first |
| Session | Chat / Feed / Thinking split one story into 3 tabs | You lose context switching between them |
| Session | Controls in four corners | Remote, status and More are hard to find |
| Composer | Attach and Photo float above the input | Looks like two separate forms |

## Two ways forward

### Plan A: keep the layout, restyle it
Cheaper, but the orbit stays and the tabs stay. It would look nicer and still be confusing.

### Plan B: rebuild around a single stream
1. **Home** becomes three groups: *Needs you*, *Working*, *Recent*, each card fully clickable.
2. **Session view** merges Chat, Feed and Thinking into one stream. Tool calls become short plain-language rows like *Edited 3 files* that expand to details.
3. **Header** holds everything you act on: status, Catch me up, model, Remote, overflow.
4. **Composer** gets attach and photo icons *inside* the field, with Send as the only primary button.

Plan B touches about 8 files and deletes [[src/home/Orbit.tsx]] entirely. I recommend B.

Nothing is changed yet. Tell me which plan and I'll start.

stream.text: Plan B. Keep the status words next to the dots, never colour alone.

stream.markdown: First pass is in. The new card always pairs the dot with a word, so status never depends on colour: ```tsx export function SessionCard({ session, onOpen }: Props) { return ( ) } ``` The whole card is the click target, so there's no tiny *Open session* button to hunt for. I also added the rule to [[docs/NEXUS_UI_NORMS.md]] so future screens follow it.

stream.text: Today · 11:26 PM
Looks better. Now remove the orbit completely and make sure the cards fit on a phone.

stream.summary: Checked what still imports Orbit before deleting it
stream.text: Orbit is imported in two places: HomeView and a snapshot test. Deleting it means updating the test too. On phone the grid should collapse to one column with 44px rows.

stream.markdown:
The orbit is gone. Here's the core of the HomeView change:

```diff
@@ src/home/HomeView.tsx
-import { Orbit } from "./Orbit"
+import { SessionCard } from "./SessionCard"
 
 export function HomeView({ sessions }: Props) {
-  return <Orbit projects={projects} featured={sessions.slice(0, 2)} />
+  const groups = groupByAttention(sessions)
+  return groups.map((g) => (
+    <Section key={g.id} title={g.title}>
+      {g.items.map((s) => <SessionCard key={s.id} session={s} />)}
+    </Section>
+  ))
 }
```

On phone the grid drops to a single column and each row is at least 44px tall.

stream.text: You were away for 18 minutes
Run the tests and tell me what's left. Don't touch the session store yet.

stream.summary: Separated the real failure from a stale snapshot
stream.text: The failing test is home.test.tsx > renders sections. Its snapshot still contains the orbit markup, so it's expected. While reading the store I noticed sessions are sorted by creation time, not attention. The user said not to touch the store, so I'll report it and ask.

stream.markdown:
## Test run

| Suite | Passed | Failed | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | 1 | 0 | 6.2s |
| unit | 41 | 0 | 3.8s |
| home | 6 | 1 | 1.1s |

The **1 failure** is the old home snapshot, which still contains orbit markup. Updating it is a one-liner: `pnpm test -u home`.

I also found something I did **not** change, as you asked: the session store sorts by creation time, so a session that needs you can sit below three finished ones. The view re-sorts it, but the phone notification order comes straight from the store.

stream.question: Should I fix the sort order in the session store, or only re-sort in the view?
